question: Two cyclists, M and N, start from the same point on a 1500 m circular track, cycling in opposite directions. M cycles at 18 km/hr and N at 22 km/hr. How long (in seconds) will it take for them to meet?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 18 + 22 = 40 km/hr = 40 × (5/18) = 100/9 m/s.

Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed.

Time = 1500 ÷ (100/9) = 1500 × 9 ÷ 100 = 135 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 135 seconds.**
